head: ec837edd7598a8b8350992275d34b782b3b5de03
reasons: plugin/hooks/shell_guard.py's git-verb detection in _part_targets (the `elif headl == "git" and len(words) >= 2:` branch, around lines 370-376) reads the subcommand from a fixed position, `words[1]`, with no flag-skipping (unlike cp/mv/rm/tee, which all run `_nonflag` first). Real `git` accepts global options before the subcommand -- `-c <name>=<value>`, `--git-dir=<path>`, `--work-tree=<path>`, `-C <dir>` combined with a further flag, etc. -- several of which consume a following token. `git -c core.fileMode=false rm CLAUDE.md` tokenises to words = ["git","-c","core.fileMode=false","rm","CLAUDE.md"]; `sub = words[1].lower()` is `"-c"`, matches neither "checkout" nor "restore"/"rm"/"mv"/"apply", so _part_targets returns no candidate at all for this part and decide() reaches Decision.allow() -- while the real `git rm CLAUDE.md` genuinely deletes/stages-deletes the guardrail file. The same bypass works with `git --git-dir=.git rm CLAUDE.md`, or `git -c x=y checkout -- CLAUDE.md` (the `sub == "checkout" and "--" in words` check also requires sub to literally be "checkout" at words[1]). None of these use a non-literal token ($VAR/$()/glob), so the fail-closed rule never fires either; they are ordinary, literal git invocations that plugin/ci/settings.ci.json's allow-list already permits bare (`Bash(git *)`).

The same fixed-position assumption also defeats _inner_shell_command (lines 235-238): it only recognises the exact adjacent pair (words[0], words[1]) in _INNER_SHELL_PAIRS (e.g. ("bash","-c")). `bash --norc -c 'echo x > CLAUDE.md'` or `sh --posix -c '...'` tokenises with an extra flag between the interpreter and `-c`, so the pair lookup fails, the quoted inner command is never recursed into, and the write idiom inside the quotes (headl would be "bash", which _part_targets does not otherwise recognise) is invisible to the hook -- again with a fully literal command and no non-literal token to trip the fail-closed rule.

This is the same class of vulnerability intent.md and this change exist to close (an unattended Bash call reaching a guardrail file while the path-based gate sees nothing), reopened through a different, untested argument-ordering vector inside the very hook meant to close it -- the same shape as the git -C chain-leak bug the previous round escalated and this round's commit 3a90bd0 fixed (confirmed below), except this one is still present at HEAD. In CI the sandbox.filesystem.denyWrite layer would still catch the actual write (spec.md Flagged concerns: the sandbox governs git as a child process), but spec.md's own Flagged concerns say a by-hand run, native Windows, or any host with no sandbox has 'the hook alone' -- on such a host this bypass is complete and silent, exactly like the chain-leak bug that was just escalated for the identical reason.

No test in the diff or in tests/test_hooks.py exercises a git invocation with any global option before the subcommand, or an inner-shell interpreter call with a flag between the interpreter and `-c`/`/c`/`-Command`; the full suite as written passes unchanged with both gaps present, so this is not a weighed-and-accepted residual (plan.md's named residual is 'an unlisted wrapper, content decoded and piped to an interpreter' -- a different shape from a documented git/shell flag shifting a recognised idiom's argument position) -- it was missed, not accepted.

Verified, separately, that the previously escalated finding (git -C's directory change leaking into a later chain part) is correctly fixed in this HEAD: _resolution_walk's `git_c is not None` branch (shell_guard.py lines 416-430) now computes a part-local `base`/`base_nl` and no longer reassigns the shared `current`/`nonliteral` that the rest of the chain loop reads; traced `git -C docs status && echo x > CLAUDE.md` by hand through the new code and it now resolves `CLAUDE.md` against the real cwd (denied), matching the new test tests/test_hooks.py::test_shell_guard_git_dash_c_does_not_leak_into_a_later_chain_part and the sibling test_shell_guard_resolves_a_git_dash_c_target (chain-local case). This part of the fix is sound and is not grounds for escalation on its own.
classification_reasons: Spec is explicit that no open concern here is fully closed: Flagged concerns accept a residual heuristic-parsing gap outside CI, and the newly found git/inner-shell argument-position gap sits inside that same accepted-but-unenumerated residual category, widening it beyond what was named.

Blast radius is wide: shell_guard.py runs on every Bash/PowerShell call in every phase, by hand and in CI; sdlc.yaml risk_list item 'auth' is touched end to end; the change's own Acceptance and eval case (0002, created at phase (e)) rest on this hook's git-verb and inner-shell detection being correct, which this review found it is not in two documented cases.

No pre-existing test exercised a Bash/PowerShell write to a guardrail file before this change (the whole behavior is new), and the new tests still leave both an argument-ordering bypass of the git-verb branch and of the inner-shell recursion unexercised.
attempted: Intent: shell_guard.py, the hooks.json registration and the sandbox denyWrite block target the Bash/PowerShell bypass intent.md describes. On-target in shape; see Proof/Tests for where the git-verb and inner-shell detection still falls short of 'every other place with the same pattern' (intent's Proposed outcome).

Spec and plan: confirmed plan.md's Files-that-change list matches the diff's files; Order of work steps 1-7 are represented; step 8's literal pytest/ruff/compileall paste is absent from this diff but per the brief this is a CI session where the runner produces those logs after the session, not something to cite against the change.

Proof: read plugin/hooks/shell_guard.py's full tokenizer, git -C handling, and git-verb/inner-shell dispatch line by line against real shell/git semantics (not the author's description). Confirmed the previously escalated git -C chain-leak is fixed by tracing the new `base`/`base_nl` locals through _resolution_walk and matching it to the new test. Found, independently, that the git-verb branch of _part_targets and _inner_shell_command both assume a fixed token position for the subcommand/pair, which a real, documented global flag (git -c/--git-dir=/--work-tree=, or an interpreter flag like bash --norc) defeats without needing any non-literal token.

Blast radius: the new hook still runs on every Bash/PowerShell call everywhere; the gaps found are reachable with CI's own allow-listed `Bash(git *)` and are mitigated only by the sandbox layer in CI, not by hand or on native Windows, per spec.md's own Flagged concerns.
Policies: security-baseline's reuse requirement and coding-standards rule 4 (no weakened pre-existing test) are both honored; the finding is a logic/coverage defect in new code, not a skipped policy.

Tests: walked through whether the full test suite as written could pass with each bug present (angle 6) -- yes for both: no test places a global git option before a recognised subcommand, and no test places a flag between an inner-shell interpreter and its `-c`/`/c`/`-Command` token.
